# RDS on an FM broadcast composite

Fourteen RDS groups on a suppressed 57 kHz subcarrier, riding an FM composite with a
1 kHz mono tone and a 19 kHz pilot. 140 kS/s complex on 98.5 MHz, 6 kHz deviation. The
station calls itself **SDR FLEX**, its PI code is **0x2AF1** and its radiotext is
**SDR RDS**.

**Nobody transmitted this.** It is generated by `fixtures/make.mjs` from a fixed seed,
using `rdsGroups` and `rdsMpx` in `web/test/support/modulate.mjs` — the offset words and
the CRC from IEC 62106, differential encoding, biphase symbols, and a suppressed-carrier
subcarrier. `SDR FLEX` is not a broadcaster and 0x2AF1 belongs to nobody; under the North
American rules it would translate to a callsign, and the fixture runs in the European
mode where it does not. Regenerating produces a byte-identical file.

The check is two-sided. The modulator was written against the specification and redsea
was written against the specification, and neither was written against the other — so a
mistake in the checkword polynomial, the offset words, the differential encoding or the
biphase convention makes them disagree instead of agreeing wrongly.

## What is deliberately absent

**There is no 38 kHz stereo subcarrier**, and the station's own decoder-identification
bit says it is mono. A fixture that claimed stereo in its metadata and did not transmit
it would be a fixture that lies about the signal it is, and the tool's whole argument is
that a displayed value is evidence rather than a claim. Open this capture, put an FM
demod on it and read it on the frequency axis ([ADR-0036](../../docs/adr/0036-a-domain-is-a-view-parameter.md)):
the pilot is at 19 kHz, RDS is at 57 kHz, and 38 kHz is empty.

## Why it is the size it is

RDS is slow and this capture is mostly the protocol's own latency. A group is 104 bits
at 1187.5 bps — 87.6 ms — and a receiver will not commit to an eight-character name until
all four of its segments have arrived twice, which is twelve groups. At the same time the
57 kHz subcarrier has to survive, so the capture rate cannot go below about 130 kS/s.
1.24 seconds at 140 kS/s in cu8 is 338 kB, which is inside ADR-0025's cap with a little
room and would not be at the 171 kS/s redsea prefers.
